dedupe_keys.name: remotely sensed above ground storage tank dataset for the contiguous us 130 000 tanks duke university 2024

description: This dataset maps over 130,000 above-ground storage tanks across the contiguous United States, annotated by hand on high-resolution aerial imagery so that it can be used directly as an inventory or to train object detection models. Each tank has geospatial coordinates, border vertices and a diameter and belongs to one of five classes: external floating roof tanks, closed roof tanks, spherical pressure tanks, sedimentation tanks and water towers. The annotations cover 2,132 National Agriculture Imagery Program tiles from 48 states taken after 2018 at 60 cm resolution or finer, chosen near known refineries, terminals and gas processing plants, and the imagery, inventory and tile characteristics total 2.3 GB. It was produced by Celine Robinson, Kyle Bradbury and Mark E. Borsuk at Duke University and published in a data article in January 2024. Coverage is national. The article is free under CC BY 4.0, and all components are available to download from a public repository. Caveats: tiles were selected where infrastructure was expected, so tanks elsewhere are missed, small tanks were harder to identify, and contents and operators are not given. For simulation it locates tanks holding petroleum, chemicals and water, useful for Natech flood and storm surge exposure, storage capacity and supply disruption studies. It is related to the EPCRA Tier II hazardous chemical inventory reports record in this catalogue, which describes what facilities store. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (figshare records).
